evidence_set: Studies requiring more than 72 hours of abstinence before testing (k = 15; n = 928) found d −0.08 (95% CI −0.22 to 0.07; P = .29), smaller than studies requiring 72 hours or less, none or unstated included (k = 54; n = 7,799; d −0.30, −0.37 to −0.22); chi-square 6.36, P = .01. Longer mean reported abstinence (k = 28; n = 1,661) went with smaller differences (beta 0.059; P = .04, uncorrected; unit of the beta not stated). Figure 3 also plots the studies reporting no abstinence or not specifying it (k = 22) and 1 to 72 hours (k = 32) separately, to show that the zero or unknown abstinence studies do not drive the difference. A comparison between studies, not a change within the same people; the more-than-72-hours interval includes no difference and reaches −0.22, close to the overall estimate of −0.25, which lies just outside it.

evidence_set: The Methods say never use was always the reference, but Table 1's reference rows include no cannabis within the last year (Wiles et al.), no cannabis use at age 18 (Arseneault et al.) and none or no use for frequency at baseline (Henquet et al.; Degenhardt and Hall). Swedish conscripts of 1969 (ref. 15, Zammit et al., 2002), inpatient admission for schizophrenia (ICD-8 and ICD-9) by lifetime frequency of use: 215 cases among 36,429 men who had never used cannabis and 28 among 731 who had used it more than 50 times (crude odds ratio 6.71); when use was recorded and follow-up length not stated in this source. Editors' calculation: crude proportions 0.59% (about 6 in 1,000) and 3.8% (about 38 in 1,000), nothing adjusted. Five of the six pooled cohorts are cohorts that Moore et al. (2007) also pooled, four through the same reports (Tien and Anthony 1990, ECA; Arseneault 2002, Dunedin; Zammit 2002, Swedish conscripts; Wiles 2006, NPMS); for the German EDSP cohort Marconi cites a different 2005 paper (ref. 13, Henquet, Murray, Linszen and van Os, Schizophrenia Bulletin) from Moore's (ref. 25, Henquet, Krabbendam, Spauwen et al., BMJ); editors' cross-check of the two reference lists.
